title: Sync and fulfillment resilience: data-integrity and retry-safety hardening

acceptanceCriteria.description: Every terminal lifecycle command persists order state, immutable source evidence, exact fulfillment-line claims, package work, and inventory-deduction intent in one backend-owned transaction; forced rollback plus retry cannot leave partial state or duplicate work.

Shipment, label, sync, import, webhook, manual, and marketplace callers provide shipment-scoped exact fulfillment facts or an explicit review-only unavailable result; mutable whole-order quantities never create inventory intent, and repeat settlement is a no-op.

Shopify and direct label purchase use durable fail-closed intent, reject unsafe or cross-order operator proof, prevent a second purchase after an acknowledged-but-unpersisted result, and fence stale repeated resolution.
ShipStation confirmation retry re-reads upstream shipped truth and leaves the marketplace notification spy at one call after simulated local-settlement loss.

Inventory recovery remains ledger-idempotent and kill-switch governed; the bounded recent production dry-run reported 672 of 672 shipped lines and 881 of 881 units represented, with zero missing orders and no apply.

The nine production provider-pending health facts are safely classified read-only: all nine have durable provider receipts on active outbound shipments, across eight orders and three inactive jobs, and unresolved label-purchase-intent count is zero.

The focused PS-424 lifecycle, PS-426 worker-leadership, and PS-432 resilience suites, all 45 mandatory source-of-truth guards, strict TypeScript checks, and production frontend build pass at the exact reviewed SHA.

Shipped/cancelled protections and the inventory kill switch are not weakened; closure performs no production write, label purchase or void, postage charge, marketplace notification, inventory movement, or automatic retry.

Exactly one worker owns the ShipStation stately consumers; active-job handoff, PostgreSQL connection loss, fallback ping detection, retry cancellation, and idempotent shutdown reacquire or release leadership without concurrent provider work.

sotBypass.details: Terminal lifecycle truth, exact fulfillment facts, inventory movement, purchase intent, confirmation settlement, provider notification idempotency, and worker leadership remain in named backend owners. Routes and adapters translate or pass intent; the frontend owns none of these decisions.

evidence.proves: The additive 0070 schema and canonical lifecycle command run against a migrated PostgreSQL-compatible fixture. Two shipments claim only their exact quantities; Shopify partial fulfillment uses fulfillment-order quantities rather than mutable order totals; void-before-deduction, void-after-deduction, changed-quantity relabel, concurrent retries, stale writers, and injected transaction rollback preserve one append-only receipt and no duplicate inventory or package effect. Explicitly unavailable facts create review-only lifecycle evidence and no inventory outbox.

Provider-free behavioral proof covers two-worker exclusion, active-job handoff, immediate PostgreSQL onclose ownership loss, fallback ping loss detection and reacquisition ordering, retry/timer cancellation, and idempotent shutdown. One hundred foreground admission samples stayed below 500 ms with zero database connections and zero provider calls.

Real canonical owners execute against a current-schema PostgreSQL-compatible fixture: rollback removes both status and intent, retry commits one pair, concurrent duplicate intents retain one durable row, torn confirmation projections reconverge once, and repeat operations have no second effect.

A Shopify retry is blocked before a second purchase-spy call; cross-order shipment proof and no-label proof conflicting with an active shipment are rejected; a stale terminal resolver is rejected; and ShipStation retry keeps marketplace notifications at one.

Injected transaction failure, provider-ACK/local-persistence loss, torn succeeded projection, and confirmation-ACK/local-settlement loss recover without missing intent, duplicate purchase, duplicate notification, or stale overwrite.

migrations.rollbackPlan: Revert the packet, PS-426 leadership, and PS-424 runtime commits before redeploying while leaving the additive lifecycle receipt and claim tables intact. The pre-change runtime ignores those sidecars, so rollback never drops append-only evidence or rewrites historical shipped/cancelled meaning.

rollback.strategy: Redeploy the prior runtime after reverting 12223760bf20fd867bc820de98194d11fbbd1d3e, 0c8246f7ad21419b3af43a9335a78b1cc3cf0f9e, f568bc5f0ba7bbfa0124b28b9c8503b0294e11bb, and 86f5dfe93c87d21597bcbd009d9e10934c68813d in that order. Keep additive 0070 sidecars and durable receipts; never delete lifecycle, shipment, intent, outbox, inventory-ledger, or package-ledger history and never mutate shipped/cancelled production records. The integration's injected exception proves the authoritative transaction rolls back all new lifecycle writes before a safe retry.

liveVerification.reason: The previous nine-item provider ambiguity is closed by a production READ ONLY aggregate query: every stale Print Queue sidecar has a durable active shipment provider receipt and no unresolved label-purchase intent exists. /health/deep still reports the conservative stale sidecar count, but automatic recovery is fenced and no provider outcome remains unknown. No provider call or production write was required or performed.

caveats.description: Nine historical Print Queue sidecar states remain conservatively visible to deep health, but read-only canonical shipment evidence classifies all nine provider outcomes as already durably successful. No replay or label purchase is allowed; metadata cleanup, if desired, belongs to the Print Queue operational workflow.
